quote.translation: Primal contingency is what was caught as the last idea from the empirical-hypothetical standpoint, which proceeds "from below", and absolute necessity is what was set up as the first concept from the metaphysical-disjunctive standpoint, which proceeds "from above".

regions.text: それ故に絶對形而上的必然は絶對者の謂はば肯定的性格を表はし、原始偶然は謂ばば否定的性格を表はしてるる。

quote.translation: Absolute metaphysical necessity consequently expresses what we might call the affirmative character of the absolute, and primal contingency its negative character.

regions.text: 絶對形而上約必然は絶對者の即自態である。原始偶然は絶謝者の中にある他在である。

quote.translation: Absolute metaphysical necessity is the in-itself of the absolute; primal contingency is the otherness within the absolute.

regions.text: 絕對約形面上的必然を神前實在と考へ、原始偶然を世界の端初または墜落（Zufall=AbEalf）と考へることの可能性もここに起因してゐる。絶對的必然は絶對者の静側面であり、原始偶然は動的側面であると考へても差支ない。

quote.translation: Here too lies the possibility of thinking absolute metaphysical necessity as divine reality, and primal contingency as the beginning of the world or as a fall (Zufall=Abfall).

regions.text: 「講事物の最初のものは端約に必然釣なものである。

quote.translation: There is no harm in thinking that absolute necessity is the static side of the absolute and primal contingency its dynamic side.
